Enrollment Options

If you are applying to Texas Tech K-12's tuition-free program and are a Texas resident, please note that enrollment is limited. State law requires a lottery system to select students for admission each semester.

What if my child is not selected in the lottery?

Step 1: You’ll be placed on a waitlist. If a spot opens, you’ll be contacted via email or phone. You can also try again in the next lottery.

Q: How does only ranking the Top 10% benefit students in the top quarter of students who are very close to the Top 10%?

When a student does not have a rank, a college will conduct a holistic review of the student's college application, examining the rigor of courses taken, grades received, SAT/ACT scores, and other factors. This is beneficial to Texas Tech K-12 students just outside the Top 10% because these students, along with many other districts' students, have high grades, high test scores, and strong academic and extra-curricular achievement. Many colleges generate a rank based on these factors. School counselors of other high performing schools that do not rank, report the college assigned rank tends to be higher than the high school generated rank would have been.

Tuition-Free Application and Lottery Information

2026 - 2027

If you are applying to Texas Tech K-12's tuition-free program and are a Texas resident, please note that enrollment is limited. State law requires a lottery system to select students for admission each semester. The next lottery will take place on October 29, 2026.

First Semester: Course enrollments open Aug. 3, 2026 with courses starting Aug. 3, 2026. We recommend starting early to maximize success and take breaks. Courses must be completed by Jan. 15, 2027.

Second Semester: For current students, course enrollments open December 16, 2026. For new students, course enrollments will open January 4, 2027. Courses must be completed by June 30, 2027.

Q: How does this impact admissions to universities?

In high performing school districts like Texas Tech K-12, students who rank outside of the top 10% would normally rank very high at other districts. This can hurt our students in college admissions. If a student has been given a rank by a high school, for example, the 40th percentile, many universities will use that rank as a shortcut to evaluate the student and say that student falls in the top 40% of all applicants to the university. However, if the student does not have a high school rank, the university will evaluate the student's record and assign them a rank relative to other applicants.When compared to other college applicants, our students tend to be more qualified than those who graduate with a similar ranking at other high schools. According to other Texas districts, schools saw a 38% increase in acceptance to the University of Texas and a 49% increase to Texas A&M after eliminating class rank.

When does the school year start?

Step 1: Students can apply during the posted lottery window and start courses at the beginning of the fall semester or spring semester of the tuition free program.

How is attendance tracked in an online school?

Step 1: Attendance is based on progress in your child’s courses.

Step 2: Your child must complete 5% of each course's assignments each week. For example, if a course has 20 assignments, at least one should be completed each week.

Step 3: Courses must be completed within the designated tuition free program semester timeline.

Step 4: Students must stay enrolled in at least four courses.

Characteristics Related to Potential Giftedness

There are certain student characteristics related to potential giftedness that can be more reliably appraised by teachers, parents, and others who have extended opportunities to observe students than by tests or formal instruments. Some of the more important ones are:

Step 1: Student’s use of language. This includes such things as range of vocabulary, precision in the use of words, and complexity of sentence structure. Although these can be appraised in a test situation, one obtains a better appraisal of the level of habitual use of language through observation in a wide variety of everyday situations.

Step 2: Quality of students’ questions. Most children ask questions, and some children ask many questions. Although it is true that bright children typically ask many questions, it is the quality rather than the number of questions that discriminates most sharply between the potentially gifted child and other children. One wants to look at the unusualness of a question in relation to age or grade or the insightfulness of a question, i.e., indications that the individual has grasped the central nature of the phenomenon, or indications that the individual is relating the present task or situation to other experience.

Step 3: Quality of examples, illustrations, or elaborations that a student used in explaining something or in describing events or in telling stories. Not only do exceptional students have a good command of language, but they also tend to use examples that are apt and original or to produce unusual analogies to illustrate points. Some students show an unusual ability to translate verbal materials into pictorial modes or models or schematic diagrams. All these behaviors indicate a high level of understanding of the material that the students are using, ability to communicate ideas, and originality.

**STAAR EOC Exam Requirements for International (India-Based) Supplemental Students**

- **Supplemental/Part-Time Students:**  
  If Utkarsh is enrolled as a supplemental (part-time) student with TTU K-12 and remains enrolled at his local school (not as a full-time diploma student), he is **not required** by TTU K-12 to sit for Texas state STAAR End-of-Course (EOC) exams.

- **Credit Awarding:**  
  Semester credit for TTU K-12 supplemental courses is awarded based on:
  - Completion of all course assignments, assessments, and discussion activities in Canvas.
  - Passing the online proctored final exam via Proctorio.

- **In-Person Testing:**  
  In-person STAAR EOC exams are a requirement for students enrolled full-time in the tuition-free Texas Tech K-12 program as Texas residents, but **not for international supplemental students**.

- **Local School Requirements:**  
  If Utkarsh’s future in-person school (where he plans to enroll for Grade 11) has specific requirements for credit transfer or state testing, he should confirm with that school in advance to ensure a smooth transition.

**Summary Table**

| Enrollment Type         | STAAR/EOC Required? | Credit Awarded By                |
|------------------------|---------------------|----------------------------------|
| Supplemental/Part-Time | No                  | Canvas coursework & Proctorio exam |
| Full-Time (TX Resident)| Yes                 | Canvas + STAAR/EOC               |

**Next Step:**  
- Confirm with the future in-person school about their credit transfer policies.
- For TTU K-12 supplemental courses, Utkarsh’s credits will be based entirely on his online coursework and proctored final exams.

For further clarification, contact TTU K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**STAAR EOC Exam Requirements for International/Out-of-State Students**

- **STAAR EOC Requirement**: Texas Tech K-12 full-time students are generally required to participate in State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness (STAAR) End-of-Course (EOC) exams as a condition of enrollment and for graduation under the Foundation High School program.
- **Location Considerations**: 
  - If a student lives outside of Texas (including internationally, such as in India), they are not automatically registered at a Texas testing site.
  - Students living outside Texas must find an approved proctor to administer their STAAR/EOC exams. You should contact the Texas Tech K-12 testing coordinator to arrange for an approved testing proctor and receive more information on how to set up testing arrangements.
- **Credit Awarding**:
  - Semester credit for Texas Tech K-12 courses is awarded based on completion of all course requirements, including online final exams and assessments administered through Canvas and Proctorio.
  - However, participation in mandatory state testing (STAAR/EOC) is a requirement for students in the tuition-free program and for graduation. Students who do not participate in state testing may be moved to the tuition-paid program.

**Next Steps for Utkarsh:**
- If Utkarsh is enrolled as a full-time Texas Tech K-12 student and is living in India, he should contact the Texas Tech K-12 testing coordinator as soon as possible to discuss his specific situation and arrange for any required proctoring for STAAR/EOC exams.
- If he is not seeking a Texas diploma or is not in the tuition-free program, and is only taking courses for credit transfer, his credits may be awarded based on successful completion of online coursework and final exams through Canvas/Proctorio.
